patient_summary:
Hello there! I'll explain what happened to you and what you need to do next. You had a surgery called a left modified radical mastectomy. This means they removed your breast and some nearby tissue. You had a biopsy before this surgery, and it showed that you had a type of cancer in your left breast.

You took some medicine to help you sleep during the surgery. After the surgery, they put special stockings on your legs to help prevent blood clots. They also put devices on your legs to help blood flow.

The doctors carefully took out your breast and the nearby tissue. They also removed some lymph nodes, which are small glands that help fight infections. They made sure not to hurt any important nerves or blood vessels.

After the surgery, they put some drains under your arm and in your chest to make sure there was no bleeding. They also put sutures to close your skin and chest wall.

You will need to take some medicine to help with pain. You might also need to take antibiotics to prevent infection. The doctors will check on you to make sure you're healing well.

If you have any of these symptoms, you should tell the nurses or doctors right away:
- More bleeding from the incision
- Redness or swelling in your arm or chest
- Fever
- Pain that gets worse

Remember to follow all the instructions from your doctors and nurses. If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask. You're doing great!
caregiver_checklist: Give the patient a sponge bath with warm water to keep the skin clean.
Check the patient's incision site for any signs of bleeding.
Watch for any signs of infection such as redness, swelling, or warmth.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient develops signs of bleeding.
Schedule a follow-up appointment with the surgeon in 2 weeks.
Monitor for signs of infection such as redness, swelling, or warmth.
Watch for signs of bleeding such as oozing or bright red blood.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient develops signs of infection or bleeding.
Schedule a dressing change in 7 days.
child_explanation: You had a big bump in your breast. The doctors took care of you. They carefully took out the bump and cleaned everything. You had a tiny team of helpers put in to stop any bleeding. The doctors are watching you closely. You'll feel better soon, don't worry.
source_text: PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:,  Invasive carcinoma of left breast.,POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:,  Invasive carcinoma of left breast.,OPERATION PERFORMED:,  Left modified radical mastectomy.,ANESTHESIA: , General endotracheal.,INDICATION FOR THE PROCEDURE:  ,The patient is a 52-year-old female who recently underwent a left breast biopsy and was found to have invasive carcinoma of the left breast.  The patient was elected to have a left modified radical mastectomy, she was not interested in a partial mastectomy.  She is aware of the risks and complications of surgery, and wished to proceed.,DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE:  ,The patient was taken to the operating room.  She underwent general endotracheal anesthetic.  The TED stockings and venous compression devices were placed on both lower extremities and they were functioning well.  The patient's left anterior chest wall, neck, axilla, and left arm were prepped and draped in the usual sterile manner.  The recent biopsy site was located in the upper and outer quadrant of left breast.  The plain incision was marked along the skin.  Tissues and the flaps were injected with 0.25% Marcaine with epinephrine solution and then a transverse elliptical incision was made in the breast of the skin to include nipple areolar complex as well as the recent biopsy site.  The flaps were raised superiorly and just below the clavicle medially to the sternum, laterally towards the latissimus dorsi, rectus abdominus fascia.  Following this, the breast tissue along with the pectoralis major fascia were dissected off the pectoralis major muscle.  The dissection was started medially and extended laterally towards the left axilla.  The breast was removed and then the axillary contents were dissected out.  Left axillary vein and artery were identified and preserved as well as the lung _____.  The patient had several clinically palpable lymph nodes, they were removed with the axillary dissection.  Care was taken to avoid injury to any of the above mentioned neurovascular structures.  After the tissues were irrigated, we made sure there were no signs of bleeding.  Hemostasis had been achieved with Hemoclips.  Hemovac drains x2 were then brought in and placed under the left axilla as well as in the superior and inferior breast flaps.  The subcu was then approximated with interrupted 4-0 Vicryl sutures and skin with clips.  The drains were sutured to the chest wall with 3-0 nylon sutures.  Dressing was applied and the procedure was completed.  The patient went to the recovery room in stable condition.
